detail:
Dysautonomia International reports that its POTS Research Fund has supported more than $5 million in research, with proposals reviewed by independent experts and its medical and patient advisory boards. Funded directions include biomarkers of neuronal injury in dysautonomia, autoantibodies and sympathetic dysfunction in POTS and Long COVID, and equipment and studies measuring cerebral blood flow and network patterns across autonomic tests.

Treatment research includes a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) for immune-mediated dysautonomia and small fiber neuropathy, and a long-term POTS outcomes survey tracking diagnosis, therapy, and clinical outcomes over time. The overall direction is toward mechanism-based subtypes and controlled treatment trials rather than one-size-fits-all care.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor before considering any research study or experimental treatment.
summary: Dysautonomia International's research fund supports work on biomarkers, autoimmunity, brain blood flow, and treatment trials, reflecting how many different mechanisms may sit underneath the same umbrella term.
takeaways: funded studies probe autoimmune markers and neuronal injury biomarkers
trials include immune therapy for immune-mediated dysautonomia
long-term outcome studies track how people do over years
research participation is optional; talk to your doctor about studies
title: Where dysautonomia research is heading
